messages:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — tenant=kestrel-corp (VPC dedicated pool). tokens_per_minute spike: 4.2x baseline. Billing anomaly triggered. Pager -> #incidents oncall. Alert: https://alerts.redwood.internal/alert/1769000456

Marta: I'm taking initial lead, oncall now. Paging @Raj for runtime + tokenizer checks.

Raj: Looking at pool metrics — request size distribution shifted, lots of 30–40k token counts showing up. KV cache pressure increased, queues spiked on gpu-4. Possible encoder/tokenizer change upstream. No infra deploys from our side in last 2h.

Eli: Kestrel support channel shows they deployed a tokenizer update at 03:12 UTC (their side) — patch note: "encoding normalization switch (NFKC) + new merge table". They didn't run tokenization smoke tests against our runtime.

Marta: Ok. Mitigation plan (short):
1) Apply tenant-level rate limiter to cap tokenized tokens/request to 8k
2) Route new requests from kestrel-corp to fallback model variant with byte-level tokenizer (compat mode)
3) Engage billing to stop further automated charge accrual and apply emergency credit hold
4) Ask Kestrel to revert their tokenizer patch or provide mapping table

OpsLead: I'm applying the rate limit now (policy id: rl-tenant-kestrel-2026). Also creating gateway rule to reject >8k tokenized requests with 413. Spinning up extra compatible workers to avoid latency SLO violations.

deploy-bot: Deployment action queued: route kestrel-corp traffic -> model: redwood-compat/v1-fallback. ETA 90s.

Kestrel-Support: Confirmed — we pushed the encoder out at 03:12 and are rolling back immediately. Rolling back to encoder v1.7 now. ETA ~8m. Apologies, will follow up with full changelog.

Raj: After routing to fallback, token counts per request dropped to ~1.4x baseline. Cost rate decelerating. Attaching sample diff from logs (truncated):

```
- input: "\u200b\u202c... user text"
- tokenizer: "custom-nfkc-v2" -> produced 31284 tokens
+ input: "same text"
+ tokenizer: "byte-level-v1" -> produced 4120 tokens
```

Marta: Good. Billing — can you pause charge accumulation and create an emergency credit for kestrel-corp until we confirm root cause?

Billing: Paused automated billing for tenant kestrel-corp at 03:22 UTC and created a temporary credit hold. We'll calculate provisional credit for the spike and propose to CS. Ticket: BILL-4827.

Eli: Handing off to night oncall (@Eli) to own follow-ups, customer comms, and post-rollback verification. Marta -> you can clear once Kestrel confirms counts normalized and billing credit accepted.

Marta: Handoff noted. Key action items for night:
- Confirm rollback completed and token profiles back to baseline
- Keep fallback routing up for +1h after rollback to catch late requests
- Draft customer-safe summary + remediation steps and proposed credit
- Create postmortem stub (INC-2026-042) and assign owners

Kestrel-Support: Rollback completed at 03:48 UTC. We confirm encoder v1.7 active. We'll fetch logs and share our deploy diff within 2h.

Raj: Verifying metrics — tokens_per_request back to baseline by 03:52 UTC. GPU queue lengths normalized. I'll leave fallback routing in place for 1h, then we can switch back if stable.

OpsLead: Post-incident ops tasks: add preflight tokenization check at ingress (compare expected token count delta threshold), add Unicode normalization alerting, and require canary tokenization run for future encoder changes in VPC tenants.

Eli: I'll draft customer-facing note now and loop in Billing + CS. Suggested wording: short apology, cause (encoder normalization mismatch), timeline of actions, credit offer, next steps.

Marta: Thanks all. I'll mark incident as resolved in pager once Billing confirms credit assignment and Kestrel acknowledges.

Kestrel-Support: Acknowledged. We'll follow up with postmortem from our infra team. Sorry for the outage.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED — kestrel-corp encoding delta. Duration: 00:47:00. Pager cleared. Incident record: INC-2026-042.
